name: Dr. Beth Erickson
title: Board President, Cambrian School District
years_of_service: Joined the Cambrian School District Board of Trustees in February 2023, appointed to fill a vacancy; elected to a full term in November 2024, currently serving 2024 to 2028.
background: Erickson has been active in the Cambrian School District community since 2015, when her children began kindergarten there; she now has an 8th grader at Price Middle School and a 10th grader at Branham High School. Before joining the board, her volunteer roles included President of the Home and School Club at Farnham Elementary and Price Middle School, Treasurer of the Cambrian Educational Foundation, and membership on a School Site Council, the district's LCAP Committee, and its Budget Advisory Committee.
She holds a Ph.D. in Physical Chemistry from the University of Pennsylvania and is Director of Software Quality for LCMS at Agilent Technologies.

She joined the Board of Trustees in February 2023 to fill a vacancy and was elected to a full term in November 2024, currently serving through 2028. As a trustee she continues to serve on the district's Budget Advisory Committee and its Policy Committee. As Board President, she presided at the board's June 18, 2026 meeting when it adopted Resolution 25-26-19 calling for an election on Measure Q, a new $148-per-parcel education parcel tax, for the November 3, 2026 ballot; full detail on that measure, including the district's concurrent budget pressures (a February 2026 vote to close Sartorette Elementary School and a General Fund reserve reported below the state-required minimum), is covered in content/measures/scc-measure-q-2026.json and not duplicated here.

attendance: No individually published meeting-attendance or voting-participation record for Board President Erickson was found. Cambrian School District does not appear to publish a per-trustee attendance scorecard on its public board pages; board agendas are available via the district's meeting-management system (the June 18, 2026 agenda for Resolution 25-26-19 is cited among this profile's sources), which would in principle allow a manual tally of attendance and votes, but compiling that was not feasible within this session's tool budget, and the resolution's own agenda listing did not show a roll-call vote count.
